newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian bonds correct under weight of U.S.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian bonds correct under weight of U.S.

text.p: Australian bonds fell sharply in late trading as the market corrected the steep rally of the past few weeks and after several attempts to hold their ground earlier in the session finally caved in, traders said.

A slide in U.S. Treasuries on Friday triggered a sharp mark-down initially and while the 8.0 percent yield on the 10-year bond held for most of the day a late break of this level saw the market in quick retreat, they added.
"We've come along way without any sort of reversal at all, so this is a much needed correction," one trader said. "We closed on key support, so SYCOM is going to be interesting."
Offshore hedge fund selling fuelled the downtrend once 91.980 was broken on the September 10-year bond futures contract and saw it close at 91.920, down 23 basis points from Friday.

Bond prices had risen sharply either side of last week's budget, spurred on by Standard & Poor's revision of Australia's outlook to positive and amid hopes of a further easing in monetary policy before year-end.
Meanwhile, the Treasury announced details of its first T-bond tender of the 1996/97 financial year, offering a total of A$700 million of stock in two tranches on Tuesday.

The Australian/U.S. 10-year bond yield spread blew out sharply as the local market went into retreat, having dipped below resistance at 125 basis points in early trading. Stronger than expected U.S. July durable goods orders had sent the U.S. bond market reeling on Friday, but stabilised in Tokyo trading.

A break of 91.920 risks a further retracement to 91.830 and just above a chart gap to 91.785. On the upside the market is now dogged by a congestion area between 91.940 and 91.980. The contract touched a near 2-1/2 year high of 92.210 last week.
